items.title: John Handy Interview, 1958-12-04
items.q: I was with Tom for about, let's say five, six years. Matter of fact, I was with him from 1918 up to 1924.

ctx.x: Oh, him and Peter Bocard then used to play together on those parades. I think it was the... I think Solastain had a brass band at that time, and they were playing together, and he was a member of the band. But I didn't like that. You didn't like that? No, I didn't like that. Couldn't get me out there. I didn't want to play. Now, sometime when a musician would die like that, or René and them would get together and just build up a band. No pay, just play behind him, you know what I mean? I'd go out there, something…
How long were you with Tom Alvin? How many years?

I was with Tom for about, let's say five, six years. Matter of fact, I was with him from 1918 up to 1924. 1924. 1924, I got married in 1923. 1924, I left here and went to Baton Rouge with Titt Johnson's off string. He had one of the leading bands outside of New Orleans. It was Bud Scott out of Natchez, and Williams out of Napoleonville, Donisonville.

Well, he had a little bit of air on the piano. But play. Ooh, he could play some piano. And never was sober. Never was sober. He stayed right there in the same hotel with us. He wake up in the morning and get drunk. Get drunk when he eat. Twelve o'clock he get drunk. Go to work he's drunk. Come from work he's drunk. But play. Never was late on the job. And never went to sleep. Never went to sleep. But he'd be drunk. Played everything you put in front of him and what you don't put in front of him he played. He was…
